title: Deviation register rows and unresolvable evidence ids
cluster_summary: All four findings are documentation-only register hygiene in per-repo deviation registers: citations that do not resolve or point at unrelated findings (CM, LibKa0s), a stale per-profile-stamp row (AbsorbTracker) and wording nits (PFE). The recurring cause is cross-repo consolidation ids (WS-02, LibKa0s-A-*, cross-repo LK-29/LK-30) written back into per-repo registers, where they collide with or fail to resolve against the repo's own audit ids. The fixes land per repo as small edits to the citation cells. An optional upstream guard (audit-review-history: qualify a cross-repo plan id with its bundle path or cite the commit sha) would stop the problem recurring, but it does not make the per-repo fixes unnecessary. Do AT, CM and LK in this pass and fold PFE in alongside them once the owner confirms D9.

verdicts.assessment: savedvariables-§1 (v2.65.0) sanctions the per-profile-stamp route from OnProfileChanged/Copied/Reset, and the addon follows it, so the row overstates the deviation. Two differences remain, and whether the §1 MUSTs reach them is ambiguous: the per-profile stamp defaults to 1 (defaults/Profile.lua:68), and the lift writes the stamp itself (core/Database.lua:89). Retiring the row with no record of them would invite a future audit to raise them again.
verdicts.remediation: Narrow the ARCHITECTURE.md:375 row to what still differs: the per-profile default of 1 (the pre-v3 floor) and MigrateProfileToV3 writing profile.schemaVersion itself rather than a runner doing it. Note that the route itself is now sanctioned by v2.65.0, and keep the profiles.md link and the trigger. Alternatively, retire it to docs/recorded-decisions.md -> Retired register rows with the v2.65.0 reason, plus an explicit sentence on why default 1 and the self-stamping lift comply.

verdicts.assessment: Verified: CM-R-05 and CM-R-10 resolve to unrelated 2026-09-07 findings (colorDecode, MakeCloseButton), CM-18 resolves to an unrelated 2026-07-12 audit item, and WS-02 does not exist in this repo. A reader who follows these citations lands on the wrong evidence, against audit-review-history's resolve-every-id MUST. The rows' reasoning is correct.
verdicts.remediation: In ARCHITECTURE.md:376, cite reviews/2026-08-05 F-010 and reviews/2026-09-23 F-005 in place of CM-R-10/CM-R-05. In :377, replace 'CM-18, WS-02 ruling' with the 2026-09-23 audit/review ids or issue #39, and rewrite 'take the WS-02 route (b)' in What differs as 'route (b) of options-ui-§1'. Name any cross-repo item by its full bundle path. Leave the reasoning unchanged.

verdicts.assessment: Verified: LibKa0s-A-07/-A-10/-A-03 are cross-repo renumberings that do not exist in docs/audits/2026-09-23, and the cross-repo plan items LK-29/LK-30 collide with this repo's own audit ids, which name different findings. The citations are actively misleading in the upstream every addon reads.
verdicts.remediation: In CLAUDE.md, replace LibKa0s-A-07 -> LK-28 (row 3, :75), LibKa0s-A-10 -> LK-37 (row 5, :77) and LibKa0s-A-03 -> LK-17d (:335). Qualify the cross-repo plan items LK-29/LK-30 with their bundle path (Ka0sAddonsCommonTasks docs/2026-09-23-REVIEW_AND_STANDARDS_AUDIT_REMEDIATION/) or replace them with the commit sha. Edit no frozen record. Optional upstream follow-up in WowAddonStandards audit-review-history: a cross-repo id quoted in a per-repo document must carry its bundle path or a commit sha.

verdicts.assessment: Both rows are accepted and correct; this is wording only. The citation gap in row 2 is a SHOULD (documentation-§3). Issue #3 closed on 2026-10-01, before the owner's combat smoke passes of 2026-10-02, so the closure does not by itself ratify owner default D9. Dropping the qualifier needs the owner's explicit confirmation, which can be collected when the consolidated findings list is shared.
verdicts.remediation: Once the owner confirms D9, drop 'pending the owner's ratification' from ARCHITECTURE.md:427. In the Why cell of row 2 (:428), cite 2026-09-23 audit PFE-15 and commit 79cd225 (PF-22). Make this edit alongside the other register edits, not as a standalone item.
